text:
jess: Hey @support / @oncall — NovaHealth is reporting a sudden spike of 429s from their dedicated pool `nova-prod` starting ~10:30 UTC. Also seeing a handful of 503s. Can someone take a look? :frowning:

sam: On it. Any recent quota or plan changes for that tenant?

jess: Customer CS says they updated quotas this morning via billing UI. No other config changes reported.

alex: Quick grep of the proxy logs shows many 429s with reason `tenant_quota_exceeded`. Example lines:
```
2026-03-17T10:31:12Z proxy[reqid=abcd] tenant=novah health: 429 rate_limited tenant_quota_exceeded unit=concurrent_requests current=120 max=120
2026-03-17T10:31:14Z proxy[reqid=abce] tenant=novah health: 429 rate_limited tenant_quota_exceeded unit=concurrent_requests current=118 max=120
```
Looks like the quota unit on the tenant is `concurrent_requests`.

maria: Hmm — NovaHealth quota should be `requests_per_minute` for their plan. If the billing UI saved the wrong unit, the system would enforce immediate hard concurrent caps and could block new inflight requests even though they expect minute-based rate. That also explains the 503s when upstream gets backpressure.

opsbot: autoscaler check: pool `nova-prod` utilization=95% over last 5m. autoscale_policy=enabled but last_scale_event suppressed by `tenant_quota_block=true` flag.

autoscaler-bot: Detected: scale blocked because per-tenant quota type != pool-allowed quota types. Reason: "quota_unit_mismatch". Fallback policy not permitted for dedicated pools with tenant-bound strict quotas.

kyle: Repro steps I ran in a staging copy of their tenant:
1) set tenant quota: `{ "unit": "concurrent_requests", "limit": 120 }`
2) fire 200 concurrent requests -> immediate 429s
3) change quota to `{ "unit": "requests_per_minute", "limit": 6000 }` -> traffic flows and autoscaler behaves normally

So it's definitely a units mismatch.

sam: Can we do a temporary tenant override to unblock them while we fix validation? Suggested quick command:
```
redwood admin tenant-override --tenant novah --quota-unit requests_per_minute --limit 6000 --reason "support hotfix"
```

jess: I applied the override at 10:46 UTC (confirmed by billing log). Customer reports 429s dropped to near zero and 503s cleared within ~30s. :thumbsup:

alex: Added the relevant snippets to the incident ticket. We should add a migration/validation step in the service that rejects mismatched units on dedicated tenants or forces a conversion. Current bug: UI allows selection of `concurrent_requests` for dedicated tenant plan though runtime treats those as incompatible with autoscale and pooling semantics.

maria: Action items:
- [ ] Engineering: add server-side validation to prevent incompatible quota unit types on dedicated tenants (owner: eng-platform) — P0
- [ ] Product: remove `concurrent_requests` option from billing UI for dedicated plans (owner: product) — P1
- [ ] SRE: add alert that fires when autoscaler is suppressed due to `quota_unit_mismatch` (owner: eng-sre) — P1
- [ ] Support: follow up with NovaHealth, explain root cause and confirm SLA impact (owner: CS)

kyle: Also adding a short-term mitigation: allow autoscaler to ignore tenant quota suppression for a single manual override window (5m) when an admin hotfix is applied, so customers see recovery quicker when we do manual fixes.

jess: Thanks everyone — marking thread resolved for now. I'll update the ticket with timestamps and the override command used. If anyone wants to add logs, paste them here.
